conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during this stay. Can you tell me what brought you back to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I was just discharged yesterday, but this morning at 2 AM, I started feeling nauseous again. It happened right after I started my tube feed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And how many times did you vomit?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t know, maybe around 100 times? It was mostly white phlegm. Then my whole abdomen started hurting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds really rough. Any fever, chest pain, or dizziness?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever or chest pain. But I do feel short of breath when I vomit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. We’ll monitor that. Your vitals are stable now. We’re going to give you some IV fluids and medications for nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will you use the same meds as last time? Morphine and Ativan helped the most.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with IV Zofran, Ativan, Compazine, and a little morphine. That’s what worked before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I just don’t understand why this keeps happening.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs came back. Potassium was low at 3.6, and your bicarbonate was 21, which suggests mild metabolic acidosis. We think it’s from dehydration due to vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious? I had low potassium last time too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s manageable. We’re giving you potassium and fluids through the IV. It should correct over the next day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes me feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. No nausea or pain. My stomach still feels a little sensitive, but I’m not vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your repeat labs show your potassium went up to 6.4 earlier, so we paused the supplement, and now it’s back to 3.9. We’ll keep monitoring it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, it went too high? Should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at all. It’s common when correcting levels. We adjusted the dose, and it’s back in a safe range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks for explaining.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The gastroenterology team reviewed your case. You’ve had a lot of testing—gastric emptying, manometry, nerve studies—all showing severe motility issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and nothing’s helped much. I’ve tried so many meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. They said we’ve reached the limit of what we can do medically. The best approach now is to stick with your tube feeds and small sips if you feel up to it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s just about managing symptoms now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. They recommend continuing your current meds as needed and following up with your specialist, Dr. ___ at ___.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I see. I was hoping there was something new, but I guess I’ll keep doing what works.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to restart your tube feeds at 90 mL/hr. That’s your usual rate, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s correct. Should I be worried it might trigger another episode?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go slow and watch you closely. The team thinks the previous flare may have been from increasing the rate too fast.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Ah, that makes sense. I did try to speed it up a little yesterday morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could definitely be the trigger. Stick to the prescribed rate, and you should do better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your labs this morning look stable. Bicarbonate is now 22, so your acidosis has resolved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. And I’ve had no nausea since yesterday. The tube feed is going smoothly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Your thyroid levels are stable too, so we’ll keep you on your usual levothyroxine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad everything’s back on track. When do you think I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you keep doing this well, probably tomorrow morning. We’ll write up your discharge orders today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll make sure my husband knows.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. You’re ready to go home. Continue your tube feeds at 90 mL/hr, take your meds as prescribed, and follow up with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I start feeling nauseous again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use your PRN meds—Zofran, Ativan, or Dronabinol. If it doesn’t improve, or if you can’t keep fluids down, come back to the ER.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate all your help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’re here if you need us.
